title: Methods versus functions: when a receiver makes sense

videos.script: Lesson 24 was about where values live. This lesson gives them behaviour. {{receiver}} A Go method is a function with one extra parameter, written before its name. There is no class around it. You can put one on a struct, on a number, on any type your own package defines. {{refused}} You cannot put one on int, or on a type from somebody else's package, and the compiler says so. {{string}} One method has a special job. Give a type a String method, and fmt prints your words instead of a bare number. {{choice}} Then the real question. When should something be a method, and when a plain function? The standard library answers with a whole package of functions, and three types that have methods. {{values}} Last, methods as values. You can hand a method to another function, and you can call it through the type, which shows what a receiver really is. Then embedding again, from lesson 16, this time with methods.
